newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SIMEONE COULD FACE LENGTHY BAN OVER STAMPING INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SIMEONE COULD FACE LENGTHY BAN OVER STAMPING INCIDENT.

text.p: Atletico Madrid midfielder Diego Simeone could be banned for up to 12 games if found guilty of violent play after stamping on Julen Guerrero's leg during Sunday's dramatic league match at Athletic Bilbao.
Guerrero needed four stitches in the wound after the incident, which has produced widespread condemnation of the Argentine international.
"He did something very ugly. It's got nothing to do with sport," said Tenerife's Bosnian striker Meho Kodro, who was one of many Spanish league players to put his criticism on record.
Atletico Madrid have until Sunday to reply to Athletic's complaint to the League disciplinary committee, who will then decide what action to take.
It was not the first time that Simeone's aggressive nature has got the better of him.
He was involved in a similar incident with Guerrero last year, and Deportivo Coruna's Rivaldo still bears a scar on his hand which he says was caused by Simeone's boot in a Brazil-Argentina game.
"He's a very violent player," said Rivaldo.
Despite the video evidence against Simeone, Atletico's outspoken president Jesus Gil says his player is not being judged fairly.
"They're looking to cover up the robbery," said Gil, who believes his side were denied two penalties in the game.

Gil also recalled two of the most infamous incidents in the modern Spanish game, in which former Barcelona players Bernd Schuster and Diego Maradona were hacked down in Athletic's San Mames stadium by Andoni Goikoetxea.
Atletico coach Radomir Antic echoed his boss's point of view.

"It's a set-up, and everything's organized," said the Serbian, who also fired off another salvo in the war of words with opposite number Luis Fernandez which followed one of the most bruising games of the season.
Athletic have been fined 2.5 million pesetas ($19,000) for failing to prevent fans from bringing flares into the game.
